Where it began

Shubman Gill was born on 8 September 1999 in Chak Jaimal Singh Wala, a village in the Fazilka district of Punjab. He had a bat in his hands by the age of three. In 2007 the family moved to Mohali, close to the Punjab Cricket Association Stadium, so that the boy could train properly.

It paid off quickly. At twelve he was facing under-19 pace bowlers in the nets, and the former India seamer Karsan Ghavri was impressed enough to ask that he be put straight into Punjab's under-14 side. There he opened the batting with Abhishek Sharma, a friend since they were small boys.

The player

Gill first caught the wider eye at the 2018 Under-19 World Cup. As vice-captain he made 372 runs, among them 102 not out against Pakistan in the semi-final, and was named player of the tournament as India took the title.

His Test debut came on 26 December 2020 in Australia, and a few weeks later his 91 at the Gabba helped India to a series win. In May 2025 he was made Test captain, and he answered at once, with a hundred at Headingley in his first match in charge and then 269 and 161 in the next, at Edgbaston. Only Graham Gooch has made more runs in a single Test than his 430. By October 2026 he had played 43 Tests, scoring 3,043 runs at 43.47 with 11 hundreds, and had led India in 11 of them, winning six.

What made him special

Gill bats with time to spare. He seldom looks hurried, and his best innings have a calm about them that makes bowling to him feel like an uphill walk. The board that made him captain spoke of his temperament, and it shows in the way he builds an innings rather than rushes it. Only Allan Border before him had made two scores of more than 150 in the same Test.

If there was a slow part to his story, it was the start. Having made his debut in December 2020, he waited two years for a first Test hundred, against Bangladesh. Since then he has rather made up for lost time.

Away from the middle

In the one-day game he became the fastest to 2,000 runs, in only 38 innings, and the youngest man to make a one-day double hundred, at 23. He was the first male player to be named ICC Player of the Month four times. He also spent part of the 2022 English summer with Glamorgan, and he captains the Gujarat Titans in the IPL, where his 890 runs in 2023 won him the orange cap.

And finally

In an under-16 district match in Punjab he made 351 and shared an opening stand of 587 with Nirmal Singh. The bowlers that day are owed a sympathetic thought, and probably a long sit-down.
